title: Soft tissue dimensional changes of augmented and non-augmented human extraction sockets: A prospective study
summary:
The biology of extraction socket healing influences the outcome of implant retaind restoration and the question of need of augmentation. It is known that after tooth extraction the alveolar ridge resorbs in vertical and horizontal dimension within the first three months. Bone substitutes for socket preservation show varying clinical outcome. No gold standard is available, so its necessary to detect, whether its possible to reduce the initial resoption tendency during the healing time of extraction sockets with a porcine material. 

The interindividual variations of resorption in the vertical and horizontal dimension after extraction are known and different materials have been discussed to prevent the resorption. There is no gold standard and the evidence is heterogenous. So, the present study will provide information about the use of porcine ridge augmentation and their influence on resorption within the first three months.  
Furthermore, at the time of implant placement, a bone biopsie is taken with a trephine drill and the bone biopsy is then analyzed histomorphometrically.

interventions.name: extraction sockets will be augmented with porcine grafting material (MinerOss® XP)
extraction sockets will be not (control) augmented
